title: Suffix Instructions Staying in a Grid
description:
There is an `n x n` grid with top-left cell `(0, 0)` and bottom-right cell `(n - 1, n - 1)`. You are given `n`, a starting position `startPos = [startRow, startCol]`, and a string `s` of length `m` consisting of movement commands `'L'` (left), `'R'` (right), `'U'` (up), and `'D'` (down).

For each starting index `i` from `0` to `m - 1`, suppose the robot begins at `startPos` and executes instructions `s[i], s[i + 1], ...` one by one, stopping immediately before any instruction that would move the robot outside the `n x n` grid (or when `s` ends).

Return an integer array `answer` of length `m`, where `answer[i]` is the number of instructions the robot can execute starting from index `i`.
hints: For each suffix starting at index i, you can simulate step-by-step in O(m) time, giving O(m^2) overall—or optimize to O(m) using backward prefix-displacement hash maps!

With prefix displacements (dr, dc) from the start of s, the robot leaves the grid at the earliest index j >= i where dr[j+1] - dr[i] hits (-startRow - 1) or (n - startRow), or dc[j+1] - dc[i] hits (-startCol - 1) or (n - startCol).

examples.explanation: Starting at (0, 1) in a 3x3 grid, the suffixes starting at indices 0..5 stay in bounds for 1, 5, 4, 3, 1, and 0 steps respectively.
Starting at (1, 1) in a 2x2 grid, the suffixes execute 4, 1, 0, and 0 steps.
In a 1x1 grid, any move immediately exits the grid, so every suffix executes 0 instructions.
